newsitem.title: GERMANY: Porsche profits seen sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Porsche profits seen sharply higher.

text.p: German sports car maker Porsche AG will report a sharp increase in net profit in the 1996/97 business year (August-July) to around 100 million marks, German car magazine "Auto, Motor und Sport" reported in its most recent edition.
The magazine said that once the current business year finishes, Porsche will have sold 30,500 cars -- a figure higher than the company had previously forecast.
In 1995/96 Porsche made a net profit of 48.1 million marks on sales of 2.8 billion marks, but earned 38.4 million marks in the first six months of this year alone.
A Porsche spokesman told Reuters the profit and sales figures were "pure speculation."
Asked about the company's 1996/97 profits, the Porsche spokesman repeated a long standing forecast that the carmaker would report a figure more than double the first half net profit.
Auto, Motor und Sport added that Porsche would produce more than 35,000 cars in the 1997/98 business year.
